description: Vendor-Bank relationships for CDM/derivatives technology classification
purpose: Track vendor relationships to distinguish ARCHITECT (internal capability) from PRAGMATIST (vendor-dependent)

vendors.cdm_capability_description: Derivatives trading system with regulatory reporting; CDM module available but not core
Cross-asset trading platform; CDM integration for regulatory reporting
Elaris OTC platform is CDM-native for derivatives confirmation and settlement
vendors.notes: First verified CDM-native vendor platform for post-trade (January 2025)

vendors.cdm_capability_description: CDM-native post-trade infrastructure; powers Delta Capita's Elaris
Broad financial software; some regulatory reporting modules
Market data provider; limited CDM-specific offerings
CDM specification development partner; Rosetta DSL creator; implementation consulting
vendors.notes: Core contributor to CDM specification and tooling

vendors.cdm_capability_description: Post-trade processing; some CDM integration for regulatory reporting
Treasury and trading systems; acquired multiple vendors
Broad financial services technology; regulatory reporting solutions
Fund administration and operations; limited derivatives focus

bank_vendor_relationships.notes: Multi-year global outsourcing agreement; comprehensive scope suggests full vendor dependency rather than acceleration

architect_with_vendor.pattern: Bank building internal CDM capability AND using vendors for acceleration/tooling
indicators: Bank contributes to CDM open source
Vendor used for specific components, not end-to-end
architect_with_vendor.example: Bank with internal CDM team + Regnosys consulting for Rosetta DSL

pragmatist_via_vendor.pattern: Bank outsourcing CDM capability entirely to vendor(s)
indicators: Bank treats CDM as vendor-managed compliance

pragmatist_avoiding.pattern: Bank using traditional derivatives platforms without CDM layer
pragmatist_avoiding.example: Bank using Murex 3.1 without CDM regulatory module

rules.scenario: Vendor press release without bank confirmation
Vendor AND bank both confirm relationship
rules.action: Verify scope (outsourcing vs. tooling) for classification

rules.scenario: Bank job posting mentions vendor product
rules.action: Does not confirm adoption; only indicates consideration

native.description: Platform built on CDM from the ground up
native.implication: Bank using this vendor gets CDM capability without internal development

expert.description: Vendor specializes in CDM implementation and tooling
expert.implication: Consulting/tooling relationship; bank still needs internal capability

partial.description: Vendor has CDM modules/integrations but not core to platform
partial.implication: Bank may or may not use CDM features; requires verification

minimal.description: Vendor has limited or no CDM-specific offerings
minimal.implication: Vendor relationship doesn't indicate CDM adoption

usage_notes.trust_audit_integration: trust_audit.py VENDOR_DOMAINS list should be synchronized with this file
usage_notes.pre_flight_check: Read this file during Pre-Flight (Step 1) to understand known vendor relationships
usage_notes.classification_impact: Vendor relationships can shift classification from ARCHITECT to PRAGMATIST
usage_notes.update_frequency: Update when new bank-vendor relationships are discovered during research
